column2: Phase one. Cardboard. Nobody fires back, so take your time. Learn to move, to lean, and to read the bar at the top of your screen.
Phase two. Doors. You work one room at a time, and you open the doorway from outside before you put a foot in it.
Phase three. Hallways. Doors on both sides. Every opening you walk past without slicing is an angle at your back.
Phase four. Opposition. From here on, the targets think. They slice your doorway the way you slice theirs.
Final exam. Everything at once. They learn the door that hurt them, and the walls will not stop a round. Shoot, then move.
Fundamentals. Most people clear a corner the wrong way: they walk up to it and look, and whoever is waiting sees them first. Here you learn to open every angle one slice at a time.
Threshold. The mistake is stepping into a small room to look around. Clear it from the door: walk the arc from one jamb to the other, and step in only for the corner you could not see.
Clean shot. The mistake is hurrying the trigger with a hostage in the way. Step sideways until the angle gives you the threat and nothing else.
Opposing doors. The mistake is walking past an opening you have not looked into. That angle is now at your back. Slice the left, then the right, then move.
Locked door. The mistake is working it from the front. That line is where the rounds come out. Work it from the side of the frame.
Rear security. The mistake is trusting a room because you cleared it once. They move. Check behind you every time you stop.
Second look. The mistake is deciding early. Some armed people give up, and some raised hands are waiting. Identify at the moment of the shot.
Hostage rescue. The mistake is clearing everything while the clock runs. Open only the angles that are on your way, and accept the ones you leave.
Home defense. The mistake is holding one good spot. They learn the door that hurt them, and the walls do not stop a round. Shoot, move, repeat.
Don't hug the corner. Walk tight around it and your muzzle crosses the edge before your eyes do. Back off the wall, and slice it one step at a time.
Don't stop in the doorway. Everyone inside is already aiming at it. Open the room from outside, then go through without stopping, and check the near corners.
Don't shoot what you have not identified. Armed is a threat. Hands up is a hostage. Slice the door, look at the hands, then fire.
Don't stand in front of a closed door. Rounds come through it. Open it from the side, by the jamb, and slice both ways before you step out.
Don't walk past what you cannot see behind. Tall furniture is a corner. Slice it in an arc, from a distance.
